nodes.summary: Let $x$ and $y$ be variables, let $p$ and $q$ be predicates on stores, and let $H$ be a store-irrelevant heap assertion. Write $s[x := n]$ for the store that agrees with $s$ except that it maps $x$ to $n$. If every store $s$ satisfying $p$ has $q(s[x := s(y)])$, then the separation-logic triple for the assignment $x := y$ is valid with precondition "$p(s)$ and $H(s, h)$" and postcondition "$q(s)$ and $H(s, h)$",…
nodes.title: Assignment rule with a store-irrelevant heap assertion

nodes.summary: The heap assertion $\mathrm{emp}$ holds of a store $s$ and a heap $h$ exactly when $h$ is the empty heap, whatever the store $s$ is.
nodes.title: Empty-heap assertion

nodes.summary: A heap assertion $P$ entails a heap assertion $Q$ when, for every store $s$ and every heap $h$, if $P$ holds of $s$ and $h$, then $Q$ holds of $s$ and $h$.
nodes.title: Entailment of heap assertions

nodes.summary: Let $c$ be a heap command, let $\iota$ be an arbitrary index (any type or proposition), and let $P_i$ and $Q_i$ be heap assertions for each $i$ in $\iota$. If for every $i$ the triple with precondition $P_i$, command $c$ and postcondition $Q_i$ is valid, then the triple with precondition "there is $i$ with $P_i$", command $c$ and postcondition "there is $i$ with $Q_i$" is valid.
nodes.title: Existential rule for separation-logic triples

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a store-irrelevant heap assertion and $c$ a heap command. For all stores $s, s'$ and every heap $h$, if $R(s, h)$ holds and $s'(x) = s(x)$ for every variable $x$ outside the set of variables that $c$ may assign to, then $R(s', h)$ holds.
nodes.title: Store-irrelevant frames satisfy the frame-rule side condition

nodes.summary: Let $P$, $Q$ and $R$ be heap assertions and $c$ a heap command. Suppose the separation-logic triple with precondition $P$, command $c$ and postcondition $Q$ is valid, and suppose that whenever $R$ holds of a store $s$ and a heap $h$, it also holds of $s'$ and $h$ for every store $s'$ that agrees with $s$ on every variable outside the set of variables that $c$ may assign to. Then the triple with precondition…
nodes.title: Frame rule

nodes.summary: For heap assertions $P$ and $Q$, the assertion $P \wedge Q$ holds of a store $s$ and a heap $h$ exactly when $P$ holds of $s$ and $h$ and $Q$ holds of $s$ and the same heap $h$.
nodes.title: Conjunction of heap assertions

nodes.summary: A heap assertion is a predicate on a store and a heap: it assigns a proposition to every store $s$ and every heap $h$. Heap assertions serve as the preconditions and postconditions of separation logic.
nodes.title: Heap assertion

nodes.summary: For a function $p$ assigning a heap assertion $p(n)$ to each natural number $n$ (an address or a value), the assertion $\exists n,\ p(n)$ holds of a store $s$ and a heap $h$ exactly when $p(n)$ holds of $s$ and $h$ for some natural number $n$.
nodes.title: Existential heap assertion

nodes.summary: Let $P$ and $Q$ be store assertions, $R$ a heap assertion and $c$ a command of plain IMP, and write $\hat c$ for the embedding of $c$ into heap IMP. Suppose the partial-correctness Hoare triple with precondition $P$, command $c$ and postcondition $Q$ is valid, and suppose that whenever $R$ holds of a store $s$ and a heap $h$, it also holds of $s'$ and $h$ for every store $s'$ that agrees with $s$ on every variable…
nodes.title: Framed embedding of Hoare validity

nodes.summary: Let $P$ and $Q$ be store assertions and $c$ a command of plain IMP. If the partial-correctness Hoare triple with precondition $P$, command $c$ and postcondition $Q$ is valid, then the separation-logic triple for the embedding of $c$ into heap IMP is valid with the precondition that holds of a store $s$ and any heap exactly when $P(s)$ holds and the postcondition that holds of a store $s$ and any heap exactly when…
nodes.title: Hoare validity embeds into separation validity

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $a$ and $v$, the assertion $a \mapsto v$ holds of a store $s$ and a heap $h$ exactly when $h$ is the singleton heap that maps the address $a$ to the value $v$ and allocates no other address.
nodes.title: Points-to assertion

nodes.summary: For a proposition $p$, the pure assertion of $p$ holds of a store $s$ and a heap $h$ exactly when $h$ is the empty heap and $p$ is true.
nodes.title: Pure assertion

nodes.summary: Let $x$ and $y$ be variables, let $a$ and $v$ be natural numbers, and let $p$ and $q$ be predicates on stores. Write $s[x := n]$ for the store that agrees with $s$ except that it maps $x$ to $n$, and $a \mapsto v$ for the heap assertion that holds when the heap is the single cell at address $a$ holding $v$. If every store $s$ satisfying $p$ has $s(y) = a$ and $q(s[x := v])$, then the separation-logic triple for the…
nodes.title: Local rule for a heap read

nodes.summary: For heap assertions $P$, $Q$ and a heap command $c$, the triple $\lbrace P \rbrace\ c\ \lbrace Q \rbrace$ is valid (in the fault-avoiding sense) when, for every store $s$ and heap $h$ with $P(s, h)$, the configuration $(c, s, h)$ is safe (no configuration reachable from it is stuck at a command other than $\mathtt{skip}$), and whenever $(c, s, h)$ reaches $(\mathtt{skip}, s', h')$ in finitely many heap steps,…
nodes.title: Separation-logic triple validity

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a predicate on stores and $P$, $R$ heap assertions. Write $A \star B$ for the separating conjunction of heap assertions $A$ and $B$ (the heap splits into two disjoint parts satisfying $A$ and $B$, respectively, at the same store), and $p \land P$ for the heap assertion that holds at store $s$ and heap $h$ when $p(s)$ and $P(s, h)$ both hold. Then $(p \land P) \star R = p \land (P \star R)$.
nodes.title: Pulling a store fact out of a separating conjunction

nodes.summary: For heap assertions $P$, $Q$ and $R$, write $A \star B$ for the separating conjunction of heap assertions $A$ and $B$ (the heap splits into two disjoint parts satisfying $A$ and $B$, respectively, at the same store). Then $P \star (Q \star R)$ entails $(P \star R) \star Q$: every store and heap satisfying the first assertion satisfy the second.
nodes.title: Rearranging a separating conjunction

nodes.summary: For heap assertions $P$ and $Q$, the assertion $P \star Q$ holds of a store $s$ and a heap $h$ when there are disjoint heaps $h_1$ and $h_2$ with $h = h_1 \cup h_2$ such that $P(s, h_1)$ and $Q(s, h_2)$.
nodes.title: Separating conjunction

nodes.summary: A heap assertion $P$ is store-irrelevant when for all stores $s, s'$ and every heap $h$, $P(s, h)$ implies $P(s', h)$; that is, whether $P$ holds does not depend on the store.
nodes.title: Store-irrelevant heap assertions

nodes.summary: Let $I$ be a heap assertion, $b$ a Boolean expression and $c$ a heap command. Write $I \wedge b$ for the assertion that holds of a store $s$ and a heap $h$ when $I(s, h)$ holds and $b$ evaluates to true in $s$, and $I \wedge \neg b$ for the one that holds when $I(s, h)$ holds and $b$ evaluates to false in $s$. nodes.title: Separation-logic while rule

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
